messages:
Jia Patel: Heads-up — infra CI for repo terraform-infra keeps failing on GH Actions since ~09:10 UTC. Terraform init times out and some runs show state lock errors.
Ben Huang: Same here. Root job `validate-terraform` fails on `terraform init` with provider download TLS timeouts, then `terraform plan` fails with state locked. Example errors in run: `TLS handshake timeout`, `Error: State is locked by operation 1234`.
Alice Rivera: Is this confined to self-hosted runners? We had GPU batch jobs spike yesterday morning and saw high I/O on infra runners.
Marco Delgado: Yes, these workflows run on self-hosted runners labeled `infra-ubuntu`. When GPU workloads ramp, runners hit 85-95% CPU/disk and network—downloads and cache writes fail.
SRE-bot: deploy-queue: Observed infra-ubuntu pool at 90% utilization between 08:45-10:30 UTC (autoscaling not triggered due to cap).
Ben Huang: Quick repro steps I used:
1) Kick off a long `apply` on infra-dedicated that holds remote state lock
2) Trigger PR plan on same workspace -> `terraform init` tries to download providers and sometimes times out
3) `terraform plan` then errors due to lock
Also we don't persist plugin-cache so provider fetches happen every run.
Jia Patel: Short-term mitigations:
- Enable plugin caching (e.g. `~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache`) via actions/cache
- Add exponential retry around `terraform init` and provider downloads
- Adjust GH Actions concurrency to reduce simultaneous plans on same workspace
- Ensure remote state backend TTL and proper unlock behavior
Ben Huang: Proposed actions/cache snippet:
```
- uses: actions/cache@v3
  with:
    path: ~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache
    key: terraform-plugins-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/*.tf') }}
    restore-keys: |
      terraform-plugins-${{ runner.os }}-
```
Alice Rivera: About concurrency: we currently use `concurrency: infra-ci-${{ github.ref }}` which doesn't prevent PRs from running in parallel across the repo. Suggest changing to:
```
concurrency:
  group: infra-ci-${{ github.ref }}-${{ env.TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```
That scopes to workspace (so regions can run independently) but cancels duplicate runs on same workspace.
Marco Delgado: Also add `path` to runs that use heavy GPU runners: set `runs-on` to fleet label that excludes `infra-ubuntu` for GPU jobs, or move CI to hosted runners for infra repos. Another idea: tag long-running apply workflows with `allow-stalled-locks: true`? (not ideal)
Jia Patel: Middle ground: prefer enabling plugin cache + retry + workspace-scoped concurrency. I'll open a quick PR with actions/cache + retry wrapper and update concurrency. Also we should add GH Actions runner autoscale policy: increase max for infra-ubuntu during weekday morning window.
Ben Huang: +1. I'll add terraform backend check to fail fast if state is locked and surface nicer error to devs. Also logging: capture `terraform providers` output to help debug downloads.
Alice Rivera: For Helm flakes we saw `helm upgrade` fail with `rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded` when cluster API server was under load. Might be correlated with control-plane spikes when GPU nodes provision.
Marco Delgado: Filed issue to track control-plane API saturation. For now, PRs that only change helm charts can run with `kubeconfig` pointing to staging cluster with more capacity.
SRE-bot: reminder: open PR #432 (infra/terraform) created by Jia Patel for cache + retry
Jia Patel: Thanks team. I'll follow up with PR and a quick runbook for what to do when a state lock appears. :thumbsup:
Ben Huang: Thanks — I'll monitor runner pool and increase autoscale cap if needed.
